name: Model Selection Heuristic Registry
summary: Family-local interpretation of shared heuristics for deterministic ML model selection pipelines.

family_notes: Selects between OLS, Ridge, Lasso, and ElasticNet based on condition number, n/p ratio, and mutual incoherence.
When the irrepresentable condition is violated (mu > 1), Lasso selection consistency drops to near zero and it operates as a screening operator only; prefer ElasticNet or Ridge.
Ridge adds lambda*I to the diagonal, shifting kappa from sigma_max/sigma_min to sigma_max/(sigma_min+lambda), guaranteeing finiteness even for singular X'X.
When p > n, Lasso is algebraically constrained to select at most n features; ElasticNet overcomes this via the L1+L2 grouping effect.
admissibility_notes: Use condition number and mutual incoherence as hard gates before committing to a regularization strategy.
condition_number is shared with dimensionality_reduction_selection: high kappa may be resolved by either regularization OR PCA, and the architect must choose one intervention, not both redundantly.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when condition number exceeds 1e6 (numerically singular).
Escalate when p >> n and full SVD for condition number is computationally prohibitive; bypass exact decomposition and default to iterative ElasticNet.
uncertainty_notes: Mutual incoherence boundary (mu <= 1) is sharp for Gaussian ensembles but only approximate for real-world feature distributions.
The n > 2k*log(p-k) sample complexity bound assumes a Gaussian ensemble; for structured or adversarial designs the required n may be substantially higher.

references.title: Wainwright (2009)
references.note: Lasso sharp recovery thresholds and mutual incoherence.

references.title: Zou & Hastie (2005)
references.note: ElasticNet grouping effect for correlated features.

family_notes: Selects between squared_error, huber, and absolute_error based on residual and target kurtosis.
Residual kurtosis is more informative than target kurtosis alone because it isolates the noise distribution from the signal component.

Huber loss bridges MSE (quadratic for small errors, precise and differentiable) with MAE (linear for large errors, outlier-robust). The delta transition point must be set dynamically from the 90th-95th percentile of baseline absolute residuals, not as a fixed scalar.
MAE is median-seeking rather than mean-seeking, making it inherently robust to extreme values.
admissibility_notes: Check residual kurtosis rather than target kurtosis alone for more accurate loss selection.
This heuristic requires a baseline OLS fit to have been run first (to produce residuals). Ensure compute_residual_kurtosis is sequenced after the design matrix is available.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when residuals are bimodal rather than simply heavy-tailed: neither MAE nor Huber models multimodal noise, and mixture models or domain-specific losses are needed.
Escalate when asymmetric cost is detected (under-prediction costlier than over-prediction): quantile/pinball loss is required instead.
uncertainty_notes: Kurtosis > 1.0 threshold is empirical; the exact boundary at which OLS sensitivity becomes practically problematic varies by domain and sample size.
Huber delta is not scale-invariant: must standardize y or compute delta dynamically from MAD(residuals) to avoid arbitrary transition points.

references.title: Huber (1964)
references.note: Original robust location estimation and piecewise loss function.

family_notes: Selects between Gaussian, Poisson, Gamma, and Tweedie regressors plus appropriate solver.
Dispersion index DI = Var(y)/E(y) and Tweedie power parameter determine the exponential family: DI=1 Poisson, DI>1.1 overdispersion, power=2 Gamma, 1<power<2 compound Poisson-Gamma.
newton-cholesky computes the explicit Hessian with O(p^2) space; enforce the p <= 1000 threshold to prevent memory exhaustion.
Feature scaling must happen BEFORE linear model fitting: lbfgs and sag solvers are sensitive to cross-feature variance differences by orders of magnitude.
is_sparse from the diagnostics family drives solver selection: sparse matrices require saga for L1/ElasticNet support.
admissibility_notes: Validate that target is non-negative before recommending Poisson/Gamma/Tweedie.
preprocessing_selection must run before this heuristic to ensure features are scaled; otherwise solver convergence may fail silently.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when underdispersion is detected (DI < 1, variance less than mean): neither Poisson nor Negative Binomial fits, and specialized distributions like Conway-Maxwell-Poisson lack sklearn implementations.
Escalate when solver fails to converge after preprocessing: likely indicates a fundamental model-data mismatch rather than a scaling issue.
uncertainty_notes: Tweedie power estimation via binned mean-variance regression is approximate and can be noisy for small datasets or targets with limited range.

The compound Poisson-Gamma (1 < power < 2) interpretation assumes the target has a discrete mass at zero plus continuous positive tail; this is appropriate for insurance claims but not for general positive-valued data.

references.title: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman (2009)
references.note: GLM family selection and variance functions.

references.title: scikit-learn linear model docs
references.note: Solver complexity boundaries and convergence requirements.

family_notes: Selects between HistGradientBoosting, RandomForest, and GradientBoosting based on the bias-variance decomposition.

Bagging (RandomForest) trains independent deep trees on bootstrapped subsamples and averages; targets variance reduction. Boosting (GradientBoosting) trains weak shallow learners sequentially on residuals; targets bias reduction.
HistGradientBoosting discretizes features into up to 256 integer bins, making split-finding O(n*bins) vs O(n*p*log(n)) for exact splits.
noise_level from estimate_noise_level and n_categorical from count_categorical_features are required diagnostics. High noise favors bagging; categoricals favor HistGB.
admissibility_notes: Noise level estimation via shallow tree is a rough proxy; the bagging/boosting boundary should be treated as soft guidance, not a hard gate.

All tree ensembles are incapable of extrapolation: if the task requires predicting values beyond the training range (e.g., upward-trending time series), a linear model MUST be used instead or in combination.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when categorical cardinality is extreme (> 1000 unique values): HistGB encounters severe degradation or memory spikes; target encoding must precede the ensemble.
Escalate when the target exhibits trends beyond the training distribution: trees will flatline at the max observed value.
uncertainty_notes: The noise threshold between bagging and boosting is soft and domain-dependent; at intermediate noise levels, both approaches may perform similarly.
HistGradientBoosting's early_stopping='auto' heuristic activates at n > 10,000 but this is an implementation detail that may change across sklearn versions.

references.title: Friedman (2001)
references.note: Gradient boosting: sequential residual fitting and learning rate tradeoff.

family_notes: Recommends scaling, power transforms, and feature removal based on skewness, VIF, and sparsity.
Box-Cox transform is undefined for x <= 0; must detect non-positive values and override to Yeo-Johnson automatically.

StandardScaler(with_mean=True) on sparse matrices replaces structural zeros with dense negative values, destroying sparsity and causing catastrophic RAM exhaustion. Use MaxAbsScaler or with_mean=False for sparse inputs.

VIF > 10 means coefficient variance is inflated tenfold by collinearity; when ALL features exceed VIF > 10, individual removal offers no selective guidance and PCA from dimensionality_reduction_selection is the only viable path.
This heuristic interacts with both regularization_selection (VIF drives Ridge preference) and dimensionality_reduction_selection (severe VIF triggers PCA).
admissibility_notes: VIF > 10 is a hard signal for feature removal or dimensionality reduction.
is_sparse from the diagnostics family is a hard gate on scaler selection: never use mean-centering on sparse matrices.
This heuristic must run BEFORE linear_model_selection (solver convergence depends on scaled features) and BEFORE regularization_selection (VIF informs Ridge vs Lasso preference).
escalation_conditions: Escalate when all features exceed VIF > 10 (total multicollinearity): only PCA or domain-driven feature engineering can resolve this.
Escalate when features contain non-positive values and Box-Cox was initially selected: must switch to Yeo-Johnson.
uncertainty_notes: Skewness threshold (|skewness| > 1) is conventional: tree-based models tolerate skew well while distance-based models (KNN, SVC, K-Means) do not. The threshold should be applied conditionally based on the downstream model family.
VIF is undefined or misleading when p >= n and should be skipped in favor of direct regularization.

references.title: Hastie, Tibshirani & Friedman (2009)
references.note: Preprocessing thresholds for skewness and collinearity.

family_notes: Selects between PCA, TruncatedSVD, and no reduction based on condition number and sparsity.
PCA produces orthogonal components with condition number exactly 1, eliminating multicollinearity completely.
TruncatedSVD is mandatory for sparse matrices because PCA's required mean-centering annihilates zero-structure.

condition_number is shared with regularization_selection: the architect must decide whether to resolve high kappa via regularization (preserves original features) or PCA (projects to latent space). Both resolve ill-conditioning but with different interpretability tradeoffs.
admissibility_notes: TruncatedSVD is mandatory for sparse matrices: this is a hard constraint, not a soft preference.
If preprocessing_selection detected severe collinearity (all VIF > 10), PCA should be strongly preferred over individual feature removal.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when data lies on a nonlinear manifold: PCA will collapse classes by projecting a curved surface onto a flat subspace. Manifold methods (t-SNE, UMAP, Isomap) may be needed for visualization but are transductive and cannot serve as preprocessors for predictive pipelines.
Escalate when the explained variance curve has no clear elbow: uniform eigenvalue spectrum suggests the data has no low-rank structure and PCA will not help.
uncertainty_notes: 0.95 explained variance threshold is an industry convention, not a principled criterion. In some domains, discriminative information may concentrate in low-variance components.
PCA is a linear-only method: high explained variance does not guarantee that the retained components capture the features most useful for prediction.

family_notes: Generates intelligent search grids based on model type and data dimensions.
Alpha grids are log-spaced with a hard floor at 1e-5: sklearn Lasso/ElasticNet scale residuals by 1/(2n), making alpha sample-size-invariant and allowing standardized grids.
For boosting: the prediction f += lr * tree creates a strict inverse lr/n_estimators tradeoff; lr < 0.125 yields diminishing returns, and error typically flatlines after ~200 estimators.
model_type is determined by upstream regularization_selection or tree_ensemble_selection; this heuristic must be sequenced AFTER those decisions.
admissibility_notes: Never set alpha=0: this bypasses regularized solvers entirely, reverting to unregularized OLS and triggering floating-point instability.
If optimal parameters sit at grid boundaries after tuning, the grid itself is miscalibrated and must be expanded before trusting the result.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when optimal hyperparameters sit at grid boundaries: indicates the search space is too narrow.
Escalate when n_estimators exceeds 200 with lr > 0.125: the model may be overfitting to noise rather than signal.
uncertainty_notes: Grid ranges are heuristic starting points derived from standard tabular datasets; for highly structured domains the asymptotic behavior may differ.
The 1/(2n) scaling invariance holds for sklearn's specific cost function formulation; other implementations may normalize differently.

references.title: Friedman (2001)
references.note: Learning rate and n_estimators inverse tradeoff, diminishing returns below lr=0.125.

family_notes: Selects between KFold, StratifiedKFold, TimeSeriesSplit, GroupKFold, and LOOCV.
TimeSeriesSplit enforces a forward-rolling, causally sound validation structure that prevents future-to-past leakage. This is a hard requirement for temporal data, not a soft preference.
StratifiedKFold preserves class proportions across folds; without it, a rare class may be absent from a validation fold, making metrics undefined.

Single-loop CV for a tuned model inflates error estimates by up to 30% on null datasets (Varma & Simon 2006). Nested CV uses an inner loop for tuning and an outer loop for estimation to eliminate this bias.
is_timeseries comes from check_time_series_index in the diagnostics family. has_groups requires external domain metadata not derivable from X alone.
admissibility_notes: TimeSeriesSplit and GroupKFold are hard requirements when their conditions are met, not suggestions that can be overridden.
If the pipeline includes hyperparameter tuning, nested CV is mandatory for unbiased error estimation; the architect must wrap the tuning loop in an outer CV.
escalation_conditions: Escalate when multiple records originate from the same entity (same patient, same user): standard CV places same-entity records in both train and test, creating massive leakage that GroupKFold must prevent.
Escalate when LOOCV is selected for time series data: leaving a single isolated time-step out destroys temporal contiguity; walk-forward validation must be used instead.
uncertainty_notes: LOOCV has near-zero bias but very high variance because the n training sets overlap by n-2 samples, making the trained models highly correlated.
n <= 100 LOOCV threshold is a computational viability boundary (n model fits), not a statistical optimality boundary; RepeatedKFold may reduce variance even at small n.

has_groups detection requires domain knowledge (entity IDs, session boundaries) that cannot be inferred from the design matrix; the architect should prompt for this metadata when entity-level structure is suspected.

references.title: Varma & Simon (2006)
references.note: Up to 30% error inflation from single-loop CV on tuned models.

audit.rationale: Deterministic model selection heuristics derived from the Gemini deep research survey on scikit-learn best practices.
audit.dejargonized_summary: These are the decision rules that look at measurable properties of a dataset and pick which prediction method, error measure, data cleanup steps, and testing strategy to use without human judgment.
uncertainty_notes: Thresholds are empirically motivated but may require domain-specific calibration.

Inter-heuristic sequencing matters: preprocessing must precede linear model fitting, regularization and dimensionality reduction address the same symptom (high condition number) via different mechanisms, and hyperparameter ranges depend on upstream model family selection.

references.title: Decision Heuristics for Deterministic Model Selection in scikit-learn
references.note: heuristics.pdf research document driving all threshold selections.
